meta.titre: Statistics for Economists: averages, frequency tables and pie charts
meta.sous_theme: Mean, median, mode, range, frequency tables and charts

sections.contenu_markdown: A trader in Garoua writes down her daily sales for two weeks and wants to know a typical day, her best day and how much sales vary. Ministries and economists do the same on a larger scale with incomes, prices and population: they summarise many numbers with a few figures and show shares with charts. The GCE papers ask for the mean, median, mode and range from a list or a table, and for the reading of charts. These are mark-winning skills because the method is short and the answers are exact.

items: A fraction can be written as a percentage by multiplying by 100.
The angles around a point add up to 360 degrees.
Numbers can be arranged in order from the smallest to the largest.
Raw data are figures as first collected, before they are organised.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Measures of central tendency

- **Mean**: add all values and divide by how many there are. $\text{mean} = \frac{\sum x}{n}$.
- **Median**: the middle value after the data are arranged in order. With $n$ values it is at position $\frac{n+1}{2}$. When $n$ is even, take the mean of the two middle values.
- **Mode**: the value that occurs most often. A set may have no mode or more than one.
- **Range**: the largest value minus the smallest. It measures spread, not a typical value.

### Which average to use

The mean uses every value but is pulled up or down by an extreme value. The median is not affected by extreme values, so it describes typical incomes better when a few people earn far more. The mode shows the most common choice, such as the most popular price or size.

### Frequency tables

When a value $x$ occurs $f$ times, the table lists $x$ and $f$.

$$\text{mean} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$$

The mode is the $x$ with the greatest $f$. To find the median, add the frequencies down the table (cumulative frequency) and see which row contains the middle position.

### Charts

- A **bar chart** compares separate categories with bars that do not touch.
- A **histogram** shows grouped continuous data with bars that touch.
- A **line graph** shows how a value changes over time.
- A **pie chart** shows shares of a total, with angle $= \frac{\text{part}}{\text{total}} \times 360^\circ$.

A **percentage change** is $\frac{\text{new} - \text{old}}{\text{old}} \times 100$.

variantes.nom: Median of an odd and an even number of values
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the list is not in order
variantes.contenu_markdown: Always sort first. For 9 values the median is the 5th. For 10 values it is the mean of the 5th and 6th. Taking the middle of an unsorted list gives a wrong answer.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When values are repeated with frequencies
variantes.contenu_markdown: Add a column $fx$, find $\sum fx$ and divide by $\sum f$ (the total number of items), not by the number of rows.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for angles
variantes.contenu_markdown: Find the total, divide each part by the total, multiply by 360 and check that the angles add up to 360 degrees. A part equal to one quarter of the total has an angle of 90 degrees.

sections.enonce_markdown:
The weekly sales of ten market stalls, in thousands of FCFA, are: 12, 15, 9, 20, 15, 18, 11, 15, 14, 27.

(a) Calculate the mean.

(b) Find the median.

(c) State the mode and the range.

(d) Explain why the mean is greater than the median.

etapes.justification: The median is only found from ordered data.
Add all values and divide by the number of values.
There are 10 values, so take the mean of the 5th and 6th.

etapes.action: Find the mode and the range.
etapes.justification: The mode is the most frequent value and the range is largest minus smallest.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Mode = 15 (it occurs 3 times). Range $= 27 - 9 = 18$ thousand FCFA.

etapes.action: Compare the mean and the median.
etapes.justification: An extreme value affects the mean but not the median.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The high value 27 pulls the mean (15.6) above the median (15).

sections.conclusion_markdown: Mean **15.6**, median **15**, mode **15** and range **18** (all in thousands of FCFA). The mean is higher because one stall had very high sales, and the median gives a better picture of a typical stall.

items.erreur_markdown: Taking the middle number of 12, 15, 9, 20, 11 as the median without sorting.
items.pourquoi_faux: The median is the middle of the values in order, not the middle of the list as written.

items.erreur_markdown: For the values 4, 6, 8, 10 giving the median as 6 or 8.
items.pourquoi_faux: With an even number of values, the median lies between the two middle values.

items.erreur_markdown: Finding the mean from a frequency table by dividing $\sum fx$ by the number of rows.
items.pourquoi_faux: Each value counts as many times as its frequency, so the divisor must be the total frequency.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving the mode of a frequency table as the highest frequency.
items.pourquoi_faux: The mode is the value that occurs most often, not how many times it occurs.
items.correction_markdown: Name the value of $x$ with the highest $f$.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing a pie chart angle as the amount of money itself, for example 48 degrees for 48,000 FCFA.
items.pourquoi_faux: An angle is a share of 360 degrees, so the part must be divided by the total.
items.correction_markdown: $\frac{48000}{240000} \times 360 = 72$ degrees if the total is 240,000 FCFA.

items.enonce_markdown:
The numbers of customers on seven days at a small shop were: 18, 25, 22, 30, 25, 19, 43.

Find (a) the mean, (b) the median, (c) the mode and (d) the range.
items.solution_markdown:
Sorted: 18, 19, 22, 25, 25, 30, 43.

(a) Sum $= 182$, mean $= \frac{182}{7} =$ **26**.

(b) The 4th value is **25**.

(c) The mode is **25** (it appears twice).

(d) Range $= 43 - 18 =$ **25**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A survey of 30 households recorded the number of children per household.

| Children | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Households | 4 | 7 | 10 | 6 | 3 |

Calculate (a) the mean number of children, (b) the mode and (c) the median.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $\sum fx = 4 + 14 + 30 + 24 + 15 = 87$ and $\sum f = 30$, so mean $= \frac{87}{30} =$ **2.9**.

(b) The highest frequency is 10, so the mode is **3 children**.

(c) The median is the mean of the 15th and 16th values. Cumulative frequencies are 4, 11, 21, 27, 30, so both lie in the group with 3 children. Median $=$ **3**.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) A household spends 240,000 FCFA in a month as follows: food 96,000, transport 36,000, school fees 48,000 and rent 60,000. Calculate the angle of each sector of a pie chart and the percentage of the budget spent on school fees.

(b) The monthly incomes of five workers in a firm are 60,000, 65,000, 70,000, 75,000 and 480,000 FCFA. Calculate the mean and the median and say which better describes a typical worker.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Angles: food $\frac{96000}{240000} \times 360 =$ **144 degrees**; transport $\frac{36000}{240000} \times 360 =$ **54 degrees**; school fees **72 degrees**; rent **90 degrees**. Check: 144 + 54 + 72 + 90 = 360. School fees: $\frac{48000}{240000} \times 100 =$ **20%**.

(b) Mean $= \frac{750000}{5} =$ **150,000 FCFA**. Median (3rd value) $=$ **70,000 FCFA**. The median describes a typical worker better because the single income of 480,000 FCFA pulls the mean far above what four of the five workers earn.

items_markdown: Mean = sum divided by number; median = middle of ordered data (average the two middle values if the count is even); mode = most frequent value.
Range = largest minus smallest, and it shows spread.
For a frequency table, mean $= \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$ and the mode is the value with the highest frequency.
The median is better than the mean for describing typical incomes when a few values are extreme.
Pie chart angle = part divided by total, times 360 degrees; the angles must add up to 360 degrees.
